title: AI Budget Variance Explainer
businessOutcomes: You understand why the numbers missed, in plain English.
summary: Compares budget vs actual performance and explains revenue, payroll, expense, and margin variances in plain English.
businessProblem: Owners get P&L reports showing variances but no explanation — they see payroll is over budget without understanding if it was overtime, a new hire, or revenue shortfall.
outcome: Monthly variance narrative: what beat or missed budget, why in plain English, which variances are one-time vs structural, and recommended owner actions.
expectedOutcomes: Monthly variance narrative: what beat or missed budget, why in plain English, which variances are one-time vs structural, and recommended owner actions.
whoItsFor: SMBs with an annual budget in a spreadsheet who review actuals monthly but lack time to write the analysis themselves.
aiInputs: Known one-time events (equipment purchase, refund spike)
Prior month variance narrative for continuity
aiOutputs: Top 3 favorable and unfavorable variances explained
noCodeTools: Budget vs actual Google Sheet + ChatGPT monthly narrative
QuickBooks classes report + Claude long-doc analysis
Excel budget template + GPT variance column
lowCodeTools: n8n month-end: QBO actuals → Sheets compare → Claude narrative
Airtable budget tracker + GPT explainer field
customBuildStack: Claude for long variance narrative with line-item context
Email PDF report to owner and bookkeeper
implementationSteps: Structure annual budget in spreadsheet with monthly columns
Connect accounting for automated actuals pull
Define materiality threshold (e.g., flag variances >5% or $500)
Run first month with owner annotating known one-time items
Review AI narrative accuracy — tune prompt for your chart of accounts
Share with bookkeeper monthly as discussion starter
systemBehavior: Read-only on accounting — never posts adjusting entries
Asks owner to confirm one-time items before final narrative
Compares to prior month trend, not just budget
Explanatory only — not audit or tax reporting
risks: AI may invent causes for variances without sufficient context from owner
Misclassified chart of accounts produces wrong explanations
Budget assumptions from 10 months ago may be obsolete
Does not replace bookkeeper or CPA review of financials
